title: Contract clarity and onboarding playbook sync
topics: MSA redlines and DPA clause alignment
Pricing approval path and committed usage
summary: Procurement and legal sync to resolve a few remaining MSA/DPA redlines, confirm SLA targets for a pilot, and align onboarding playbook steps (KMS, SSO, audit logs). AE + SE presented technical/operational details; customer asked for pricing commit thresholds and data residency assurances. Action items: DPA redline, SLA matrix, pilot pricing estimate, shared onboarding checklist.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-28 15:00 UTC | Duration ~1:02 | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Priya (Aurelia - Procurement), Daniel (Aurelia - Legal), Samantha (Aurelia - VP Ops)

[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for carving out time right before the holidays, appreciate it. we wanted to run through the few open contract bits and the onboarding playbook so we get procurement sign-off and a clean handoff to ops.
[00:18] Priya: yes thanks Maya, we've got legal and ops on the line. main ask from our side is clarity on DPA obligations, data residency, and the SLA language. also pricing — our finance team needs the committed usage thresholds spelled out.
[00:35] Luca: cool, i'll start with a very quick tech posture — then we can map contract text to how the product works. we run both hosted API and private (VPC/on-prem) options; for Aurelia likely the VPC + KMS option is what you want for PHI-ish workloads, correct?
[00:52] Samantha: correct. we have a hybrid approach, some non-PHI in hosted, but core patient data flows must stay within our VPC.
[01:05] Daniel: can you clarify what you mean by "private" vs "dedicated"? those words vary vendor to vendor and our redlines try to force clearer definitions.
[01:20] Maya: fair. in our terms: Hosted API = multi-tenant, quick start. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools (single-tenant) managed by Redwood in our cloud tenancy for predictable throughput. Private = customer-managed VPC where control plane is separated and keys can be customer-managed (KMS/HSM). we'll add a definitional table into the MSA if helpful.
[01:44] Priya: yes please, a definitional table would help our sourcing team.
[01:49] Luca: noted. on KMS: we support both provider-managed and customer-managed KMS, and for the Private deployment we can integrate with your cloud KMS; we also support bringing your own HSM in certain on-prem packages.
[02:06] Daniel: okay that helps. on the DPA, our counsel flagged the liability cap tie to fees; we'd like to ensure that the cap isn't just the last 12 months fees but tied to the committed term for Dedicated. Maya, your pricing team suggested committed months?
[02:25] Maya: right — for Dedicated we usually set a committed amount (e.g. 12-months capacity commit) that becomes the reference for certain financial terms. we can add language that for dedicated/reserved capacity the liability cap references the committed fees for that reserved term.
[02:40] Priya: that feels reasonable, need to see the exact phrasing.
[02:46] [02:46] Samantha (interject): also audit logs — we need exportable audit logs for data access and admin actions for our SOC 2 and internal audits. is that standard?
[03:02] Luca: yes, audit logs are standard for Dedicated and Private. hosted customers get sampling/30-day retention by default; we can offer extended retention as an add-on.
[03:16] Daniel: can you confirm encryption in transit and at rest and key ownership for the Private option? we've had vendors say 'we encrypt' but then hold keys.
[03:28] Luca: encryption in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and at rest for model artifacts and KV caches. for Private you retain KMS control; we only have access if you opt-in for managed-keys. we'll add a KMS clause to the DPA that clarifies key control.
[03:46] [03:46] Maya: great. next, SLA. we've had a couple of back-and-forths on the 99.9 vs 99.95 uptime for Dedicated — procurement wants to understand what each tier means for latency and failover. Luca?
[04:02] Luca: 99.9% is our baseline for hosted; Dedicated/Private can hit 99.95 depending on region and architecture. important nuance: for generator workloads with high tail-latency sensitivity we recommend multi-availability routing and warm pool capacity which is part of our higher SLA offering. that comes with a higher committed spend since we reserve capacity.
[04:28] Priya: when you say "warm pool" is that the autoscaling buffer? are we charged for that continuously?
[04:35] Luca: it's an allocated standby capacity; typically a smaller percent of committed capacity. billing is modeled into the committed price — so it's not separate line-item after you commit, but it affects your committed monthly minimum.
[04:48] Daniel: procurement question — if we fail to consume the committed capacity, is there a true-up or carry-forward?
[04:55] Maya: there is usually a true-up model with annual reconciliation; unused committed credits may convert to discounted overage credit for a short period, but we can negotiate carry-forward in the SOW for pilots.
[05:08] Samantha: for our pilot we probably want a 3-month pilot with a low committed floor and ability to scale to a 12-month commit if the ops metrics are good.
[05:17] Maya: totally doable. we often do a Pilot SOW that lists pilot SLA, pilot pricing and then an optional conversion to a 12-month committed agreement.
[05:24] [05:24] Priya: okay on pricing approvals — our internal pricing committee needs a one-pager showing committed tiers, expected monthly spend ranges, and the procurement path. can you provide that?
[05:36] Maya: yes we'll provide a Pricing one-pager and a comparison matrix (pilot vs reserved vs private). we'll include sample cost per 1M tokens for each configuration.
[05:45] Daniel: also, indemnification: we have a narrow carve-out for regulatory fines and certain types of data exposure. can you accept limited carve-outs?
[05:55] Luca: we usually push back on unlimited carve-outs; we can discuss specific language that ties indemnity to Redwood's breach of contractual security obligations and gross negligence.
[06:08] Daniel: okay i'll mark that as a follow-up redline.
[06:12] [06:12] Maya: thanks. circling back to DPA — Priya, what are your must-have DPA clauses?
[06:20] Priya: data residency assurances for EU/US, subprocessor list and notification timing, breach notification window (48 hours preferred), and right to audit for the first year.
[06:32] Luca: 48 hours is tighter than our standard 72 hours internal SLA for some detection windows — we can commit to 72 hours for initial detection and 48 hours for notification post-confirmation. would that be acceptable?
[06:47] Priya: we prefer 48 but can consider 72 if there's a technical limitation, need to double-check.
[06:54] Maya: we'll flag that as a point for legal; we'll propose 72 hours with a best-effort 48 when practical and include a remediation playbook in the SOW.
[07:05] [07:05] Samantha: on SSO — we require SAML2.0 + SCIM for user provisioning. can you confirm provisioning and RBAC integration?
[07:15] Luca: yes SAML + SCIM supported; RBAC mapping to your IdP groups is supported in Private and Dedicated. Hosted requires an enterprise plan for SCIM.
[07:28] Daniel: any limitations on service accounts or privileged access? we need to map admin roles and get audit trails.
[07:36] Luca: we'll provide role templates and admin audit logs; for private we can bind to your IAM for service accounts.
[07:46] [07:46] Priya: ok let's talk process: timeline to get procurement sign-off if we provide the one-pager and the DPA redline?
[07:56] Maya: typical procurement + legal turnaround for a deal of this size is 2–3 weeks once legal has a clean redline. given holidays it's probably 3–4 weeks.
[08:07] Priya: yeah holidays will slow things, so that's within expectations.
[08:12] [08:12] Maya: i want to show the onboarding playbook steps — i'll quickly walk through the short list and Luca can add certs/ops details. Step 1: Pilot kickoff and access — create org, SSO test account, handover provisioning. Step 2: Data ingress and KMS exchange — key rotation plan, certs. Step 3: Performance benchmark (we run a 24–72h throughput & latency run). Step 4: Integration and observability — logs, tracing hooks. Step 5: Handover to ops and runbook delivery.
[08:44] Luca: adding to Step 3 — for the benchmark we typically run a mixed workload reflecting your tail-latency targets and 95/99th percentiles; we'll collect traces and recommend batching/quantization settings if you use smaller GPU footprints.
[08:58] Samantha: can you provide a sample runbook we can review?
[09:03] Maya: yes, shared artifact: onboarding-playbook-v2.pdf (drive link) — we'll drop in the meeting notes.
[09:11] [09:11] Priya: about privileged access, who at Redwood can access our environment for troubleshooting? Is there an escalation chain?
[09:21] Luca: default is no standing access; we require customer-approved ephemeral sessions with audit logs. we have an escalation chain and will list named SEs on the SOW that can be granted temporary access only with your approval.
[09:35] Daniel: please ensure the SOW references ephemeral access and required approvals; we want a clear revocation mechanism.
[09:42] Luca: that's our standard practice.
[09:45] [09:45] Maya: quick note on testing — for the pilot we can provide up to $25k in credits for initial usage; that helps with the runbook test without impacting your bill.
[09:56] Priya: credits are helpful, we'll include that in the procurement packet.
[10:00] [10:00] Samantha: are there any regulatory constraints with model logging? we need to be careful about storing raw PII in logs.
[10:10] Luca: we mask PII in logs by default for Private; for Dedicated we can configure masking rules; we'll also supply a log-retention and redaction doc.
[10:21] [10:21] Daniel: any export controls or cross-border transfer clauses we should watch for?
[10:26] Maya: Redwood has standard export-control clauses; for data residency we can specify region constraints in the SOW.
[10:34] Priya: okay good. range of practical items now: timeline, artifacts, and approvals. can we recap next steps?
[10:41] Maya: sure — i'll summarize now then Luca will add technical deliverables.
[10:45] [10:45] Maya: Recap: 1) Redwood to send DPA redline and a definitional table for hosted/dedicated/private; 2) Pricing one-pager with pilot vs committed tiers and sample token cost; 3) SLA matrix showing 99.9 vs 99.95 tradeoffs and capacity/guardrail implications; 4) Onboarding playbook + runbook + sample benchmark plan; 5) SOW pilot template with ephemeral access, KMS clause, and audit log retention options.
[11:12] Luca: Technical deliverables: a) Benchmark script and sample output from a similar customer (anonymized), b) SCIM/SAML integration checklist, c) KMS integration guide and key exchange steps, d) sample role templates and audit log schema.
[11:34] Priya: great, and legal will send any redlines on the DPA with the preferred 48/72 wording and indemnity comments.
[11:44] Daniel: yes we'll send redlines within a week — holiday availability may affect speed but we'll aim for Jan 4.
[11:52] Maya: perfect. any final questions?
[11:56] Samantha: just one — are you tracking competitors in the pitch? our sourcing asked who else you work with in healthcare.
[12:03] Maya: publicly we work with a number of health customers; on competitors: Anthropic and VendorX were mentioned earlier in smaller procurement conversations. our advantage is the unified runtime and private deployment options tailored to regulated customers.
[12:21] Priya: okay thanks.
[12:24] Maya: i'll follow up with an email that includes links: onboarding-playbook-v2.pdf, pricing-onepager.xlsx, DPA_redline_v1.docx (tracked). we'll also include a short summary for your pricing committee.
[12:38] Daniel: thanks all.
[12:41] [12:41] End of meeting notes.

Notes: transcription uses short timestamps and occasional mis-attributions; some technical terms may be slightly garbled (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cake" once). Shared artifacts referenced as links in follow-up email.
